concept.name: Neutral day
concept.definition: A Market Profile day type in which the initial balance is extended on both sides during the session: longer-timeframe buyers and sellers are both active but roughly matched, so the auction probes above and below the early range without either side taking control. Variants close near the day's center (neutral center) or near an extreme (neutral extreme).
concept.intuition: A neutral day is a tug-of-war: both sides show up, both push, and by the close neither has won.
concept.mechanics: Identified by range extension in both directions against an average-to-narrow initial balance, with two-sided trade between larger-timeframe participants mediated by day traders; the close location (center versus extreme) distinguishes the sub-types and shades the next-day read.
concept.failure_modes: Neutral days often mark regime transitions, so the balance they display can resolve violently the next session; intraday, the two-sided extensions repeatedly trap breakout traders.
concept.misconceptions: Neutral does not mean directionless noise to be ignored — the two-sided extension tells you both larger-timeframe camps are present, which is itself market information; nor does it predict which side wins next.
concept.example: The first hour spans 4,510–4,525; the market extends to 4,540 by midday, then to 4,502 in the afternoon, and closes at 4,520 near the middle — a neutral-center day.

citations.source: Marketcalls — Market Profile: Different Types of Profile Days (neutral day center / extreme)
